Slab Heave Repair in Spring, TX

Slab heave happens when water gets into the clay under your home and pushes the floor up. We track down where the water is coming from, stop it, and bring your floors back to level.

01

We find the cause before we sell a fix.

Heave is often misdiagnosed as settlement. We test for leaks and check drainage first, so you don't pay for piers that won't help.

02

Signs your slab is heaving

  • ★A hump or high spot in the middle of a room
  • ★Interior doors that stick at the top corner
  • ★Cracks in tile or floors radiating from one area
  • ★Drywall cracks above interior doors
  • ★Baseboards with gaps at the floor near the high spot
  • ★Cracks in the garage or patio slab near the high spot
03

What causes slab heave in Spring, TX

Under-slab plumbing leaks

A leaking drain or supply line keeps one area of clay soaked, and that clay swells upward.

Poor yard drainage

Flat Spring lots let water pond against the slab, and the clay at the edge takes it in.

Long wet seasons

Heavy spring rains and storms after a drought swell clay that had shrunk, pushing parts of the slab up.

High water table

Near Spring Creek and Cypress Creek, groundwater sits close to the surface and keeps clay wet.

Removed trees

When a large tree comes out, the soil it was drying out regains moisture and swells over the next few years.

Irrigation against the slab

Sprinklers and flower beds watered right at the foundation add steady moisture to one side.

04

How we fix slab heave

  1. STEP 01
    Elevation map

    Readings show whether the slab has risen in the center or dropped at the edges.

  2. STEP 02
    Find the water

    Plumbing tests and a drainage review locate the moisture source.

  3. STEP 03
    Stop the source

    Leaks are repaired by a licensed plumber and drainage is corrected.

  4. STEP 04
    Let the soil settle

    Clay is given time to stabilize once the water is gone, with readings to track it.

  5. STEP 05
    Level what is left

    Low areas around the high spot are brought up only if still needed.

05

Slab heave repair costs

Heave repair cost depends mostly on the water source. Fixing a leak or drainage problem is often the main expense.

06

FAQs

Can piers fix heave?

Piers stop settlement, not swelling. Heave is fixed by removing the water source and, if needed, leveling the low areas around the high spot.

How do I know it is heave and not settlement?

Elevation readings show the pattern. Heave typically raises the center of the slab while the edges stay put.

Will the slab go back down on its own?

Some of it can once the water source is removed and the clay dries, but it is slow and rarely returns fully to level.

Does homeowners insurance cover heave?

Policies vary. Some cover access and repair for a sudden plumbing leak but not the soil movement. Check with your insurer.
